newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW-Baxter says higher margin is sustainable.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Baxter says higher margin is sustainable.

text.p: Baxter International Inc expects to sustain a gross profit margin of more than 45 percent through 1997, compared to a gross margin of 44.7 percent for all of 1996, said president and chief financial officer Harry Kraemer on Wednesday.
In an interview with Reuters, Kraemer said, "We're pretty comfortable that our gross margin will exceed 45 percent in every quarter of this year."
He said Baxter is comfortable with Wall Street 1997 sales estimates of about $6.5 billion versus $5.43 billion in 1996.

The Deerfield, Ill.-based company is also comfortable with the First Call 1997 consensus earnings estimate of $2.36 per share, versus $2.11 per share in 1996. "We're definitley comfortable with that," Kraemer said.
In addition, he said Baxter expects sales, general and administrative expenses as a percentage of sales to fall from 22 percent in the first quarter.
"I would definitely expect our overall expense ratio decline from 1997 into 1998," Kraemer said.
Baxter's overall expense ratio was 21 percent in 1996.

Foreign exchange reduced sales in the first quarter by about two percent. Baxter expects that level of impact to continue. "On the earnings line, the foreign exchange impact will be more in the four to five percent range," he said.
"We're taking the tack that assuming the foreign exchange rates don't get better, but don't get worse, growing beyond this year in the mid-teens is very reasonable," he said.
Baxter expects growth in the low double-digit range this year, primarily due to currency impacts, he said.
Baxter posted first-quarter net income of $150 million, excluding a one-time charge, up nine percent over a year ago.
Baxter shares were off 1/2 at 46-3/8 at mid-Wednesday.

On a sector basis, Kraemer said first-quarter sales in biotechnology were in the $400 million range; in renal, $400 million range; in cardiovascular, $200 to $250 million range; and in intravenous systems, $500 million range.

In addition to benefiting from the full impact of the Immuno International AG acquisition, Kraemer said growth rates in the second quarter and thereafter will gain from having the biotechnology's sector's Hyland unit back up to full speed. It had experienced some production problems in the first quarter, but those have been resolved, he said.
Immuno enjoys higher profits margins than its new parent, but also has a higher expense ratio, presenting Baxter with opportunities to enhance margins and cut costs.
As to whether that may mean job reductions in Switzerland, where Immuno is based, Kraemer said, "I would say almost definitely not."
